items.item_text: Bachelor’s degree preferred, or any combination of education, training, or experience that provides the required knowledge, skills, and ability to perform the job.
Experience in higher education, alumni/ae relations, communication, event management, or experience in a related field (i.e., public relations, non-profit management) is preferred.
At least four years of experience in an administrative support role is preferred.
In partnership with the Director of Alumnae Engagement, develop strategies to increase alumnae engagement and volunteer opportunities with a focus on young alums and philanthropic prospects.
Develop programs for alumnae digital engagement through the College’s online networking and mentorship platform Olive Grove, in collaboration with the Digital Engagement Specialist.
Manage digital micro-engagement opportunities, including the annual alumnae letter-writing programs.
Partner with Career Planning & Resources to identify programs that strengthen student career outcomes and provide lifelong meaningful alum career support.
Coordinate with the Engagement team to develop and track metrics that assess outcomes and efficacy of programs in support of goals.
Collaborate with campus partners in planning and executing all signature on-campus alumnae activities, key regional off-campus events, and digital engagement, overseeing logistics and communications.
Serve as point person to collaborate with the Public Events team to ensure proper delegation and execution of tasks.
Serve as program lead for Camp Scripps and the volunteer planning committee, the Camp Creative Caucus.
Coordinate the development, implementation, and execution of new and existing young alumnae events, programs, and services designed to foster a lifelong connection between alumnae and the College.

Travel regularly to support regional alumnae programs and events, and work evenings and weekends as required for on- and off-campus programs, signature events, and other alumnae engagement activities.
Establish relationships with a diverse array of alums, engaging them in conversations to help inform the office’s programs, volunteer opportunities, and engagement strategies.
Serve as staff lead for several Alumnae Leadership Council committees, helping with goal setting, recruitment, meeting management, and execution.
Document and track meaningful conversations with alumnae to help build a pipeline of annual giving prospects and major gift prospects.

Partner with the Annual Fund team on Reunion class giving efforts, including but not limited to volunteer recruitment and stewardship, solicitations and communications, and Reunion class volunteers to achieve both attendance and giving participation goals.
Develop regular content for alumnae website, e-communications, and social media accounts, and work closely with the Alumnae Engagement Coordinator in monitoring and management of these platforms.
Develop strategies around online community building and leveraging the College’s online networking and mentorship platform, Olive Grove.
Active support for the College’s Principles of Community and Institutional Values in the performance of job duties.
Demonstrated success developing programs, planning and executing events, and managing volunteers.
Strong strategic planning skills and demonstrated ability to make data-informed decisions.
Strong customer service orientation, with excellent problem-solving and relationship-building skills.
Excellent professional writing and verbal communication skills.
Demonstrated success leading complex projects from conception through completion with minimal supervisory oversight and strong attention to detail.
Ability to effectively prioritize competing responsibilities, manage timelines, and coordinate with multiple stakeholders.
Ability to build productive relationships with staff and alumnae volunteers and ability to engage with diverse audiences.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office suite and social media channels (Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn)

Proficiency or willingness to develop proficiency in the division’s CRMs and other systems, specifically Blackbaud Raiser’s Edge NXT, MailChimp, Workday, Formstack, Qualtrics, WordPress, Canva, and Asana.
An understanding of small, private, liberal arts colleges, and to hold a commitment to women’s education.

pay.source_text: quired. Work schedules may vary based on the needs of the College or department. Hourly rate range: $31.51 to $33.17. The hourly rate of the finalist(s) selected for this role will be set based on a variety of factor
